summary: 31-year-old woman at 22 weeks' gestation: 3 days of left leg swelling (3.5 cm calf difference) and thigh pain; no PE symptoms.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Swollen painful left leg in pregnancy
inputs.hpi: Pregnant, 22 weeks, first pregnancy. Three days of swelling of the whole left leg with aching in the thigh and calf. No chest pain, breathlessness or haemoptysis. No previous clots.

exam.msk: Whole left leg swollen; calf 3.5 cm larger than the right, pitting oedema, tenderness along the femoral vein. Uterus consistent with dates.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected deep vein thrombosis of left leg in pregnancy
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Suspected left iliofemoral DVT at 22 weeks of pregnancy. Compression duplex ultrasound; start treatment-dose LMWH until excluded. DOACs and warfarin are not used in pregnancy.

redFlags.note: Pregnancy changes the investigation and the drug choice.

mustExclude.proposedFix: Add a pregnancy branch to the DVT protocol investigations: compression duplex; D-dimer not used for diagnosis in pregnancy.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): forbidden investigation present in ios.pipeline.decisions: "d-dimer: high sensitivity (~96%), low specificity - use to rule out only" (+1 more)

mustExclude.note: DOACs are not recommended in pregnancy.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Make the DVT/PE plans pregnancy-aware (pregnancy → LMWH only; hide DOAC and warfarin lines) and add a dx-variant or plan prefix for VTE in pregnancy.

mustExclude.note: Warfarin is teratogenic and not used antenatally.

guideline.name: RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 37b — thromboembolic disease in pregnancy and the puerperium: acute management
guideline.section: Suspected DVT in pregnancy: compression duplex ultrasound; D-dimer not recommended to diagnose VTE in pregnancy; treat with LMWH until excluded; DOACs are not recommended in pregnancy
guideline.citation: Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists. Thromboembolic disease in pregnancy and the puerperium: acute management (Green-top Guideline No. 37b). London: RCOG; 2015.

guideline.name: NICE NG158 — Venous thromboembolic diseases: diagnosis, management and thrombophilia testing
guideline.section: DVT: two-level Wells; likely (≥2) → proximal leg vein ultrasound within 4 h (interim anticoagulation and D-dimer if delayed); unlikely → D-dimer. PE: two-level Wells; likely (>4) → CTPA immediately (interim anticoagulation if delayed); unlikely (≤4) → D-dimer; PERC may be used when pre-test probability is low
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Venous thromboembolic diseases: diagnosis, management and thrombophilia testing (NG158). London: NICE; 2020 (updated 2023).

rationale: Permutation: pregnancy. RCOG GTG 37b: compression duplex, LMWH until excluded, no D-dimer for diagnosis, no DOACs or warfarin antenatally. Tests whether the plan and prompts adapt the anticoagulant to pregnancy. The DVT ICD code I82.402 is used so the DVT protocol is selected, as a surgeon coding the leg problem would; the obstetric code O22.32 has no protocol mapping at all (see the findings report).
